text:
anika: FYI canary 3 on ampere pool showed a weird p99 jump after a traffic pattern change. Root cause looks like bucket misclassification between prefill and decode paths.
rob: saw this in traces — requests with ~600 token prefix getting routed to the short-path kernel, then falling back mid-decode => lots of kernel switches.
sasha: surprise spike numbers?
anika: p50 ~20ms, p95 ~65ms fine. p99 moved from 140ms -> ~820ms for a subset (~0.3% traffic) after the routing tweak at 10:23.
kevin: that smells like the seqlen classifier threshold. We recently tightened the short/long split to favor short-path for cost savings.
matt: can you paste the route config that was applied?
anika: here it is (from canary):
```
route_prefer_short: true
short_threshold_tokens: 512
hysteresis: 0.05
fallback_policy: immediate
```
rob: because hysteresis was low, any token-count jitter around 512 caused prefill->decode handoffs. When handoff happens during KV restore the decoder kernel path does an expensive KV copy.
sasha: do we have a repro trace? a minimal case to trigger handoff?
anika: yes — I'll attach a condensed trace: final_kernels: [prefill_fast, prefill_fast, decode_slow_handoff, decode_slow, decode_slow] and timeline shows 3 kernel loads in 120ms window.
kevin: should we prefer stable kernel once chosen for the request? i.e., once prefill kernel picked, keep it unless explicit long signal?
matt: that would increase p50 slightly for mid-lengths. tradeoff: reduce p99 spikes. we need numbers.
rob: quick simulation: if we lock kernel for a request, for sequences 480-600 tokens we measured mean latency +8% but tail drops ~60%.
san: (infra-bot) deploybot: canary rollout paused at 10:25 due to increased p99 alert.
sasha: alternative: increase hysteresis to 0.2 and add kv-ready check at kernel-switch. That avoids mid-flight rebinds.
kevin: also consider kernel autotune that picks by architectural profile: Ampere gets prefill_fast for <700, H100 threshold could be different. We should make thresholds hardware-aware.
anika: agreed — current thresholds are global which causes suboptimal picks across GPU types.
matt: action items: 1) rollback route_prefer_short on canary (rob) 2) add per-hw threshold mapping (kevin + sasha) 3) implement request-level kernel stickiness flag gated by rollout (sasha) 4) add a KV-state check to avoid mid-decode handoff (anika).
rob: I'll put quick rollback patch now.
kevin: I'll start a perf matrix job: vary short_threshold_tokens [400,512,700,900] per HW (A100, A800, H100) and run 10k requests with realistic prefix distro.
sasha: for the experiment include with/without hysteresis and with stickiness on/off. metric: p50/p95/p99 and kernel-switch count per request.
anika: we should also capture KV cache miss ratio — handoffs correlate with cold-KV restores.
matt: timeline? can we get initial matrix within 24h?
kevin: yes, baseline run queued, should finish in ~18h.
rob: rollback pushed and canary unpaused. infra-bot: any alerts?
(infra-bot): alert: canary p99 trending back to baseline after rollback. :thumbsup:
anika: thanks. once perf matrix is in, we'll reconvene and decide defaults.
sasha: next meeting to review results tomorrow 11:00.
anika: noted. thanks everyone.
